proposals.rationale: TP53 is the wild-type p53 node; its knockout removes the main apoptosis trigger and also disables p21 and MDM2 regulation. AKT knockout blocks the PI3K survival pathway. Together they force the cell to rely on the DNA-damage axis, but ATM activation may still permit survival; however, this pair targets the two most central survival signals in this FGFR3-driven, wild-type p53 context.

Both receptor tyrosine kinases are active (FGFR3_stimulus=1, EGFR_stimulus=0 but EGFR can be SPRY-mediated). Simultaneous knockout removes all growth‑factor input, collapsing RAS, PI3K and GRB2 activation. This should starve the proliferative and survival signals that keep the cell alive after radiation.

explanation.summary: Knocking out TP53 forces committed apoptosis (Apoptosis_high=1) in every long-term state of this scenario. The knockout is selective: a resting normal cell exposed to the same radiation survives. The 8 steps below are each checked against the model's update rules.

steps.text: TP53 knockout sets p21CIP to zero, removing a growth inhibitor and allowing cell cycle progression.
With Growth_inhibitors absent, p16INK4a drops to zero, further relieving repression of the cell cycle.
GRB2 is silenced because SPRY is present and EGFR is off, leaving FGFR3 signaling unopposed.
FGFR3 becomes active since GRB2 is missing and the stimulus is present, while EGFR remains inactive.
RAS turns on as a direct consequence of active FGFR3.
CyclinD1 rises because p21CIP and p16INK4a are both zero and RAS is active.
RBL2 is inactivated because CyclinD1 is present, releasing a brake on E2F transcription factors.
RB1 is lost due to CyclinD1 presence, completing the removal of RB-mediated growth control.

caveats: The model assumes FGFR3_stimulus and DNA_damage are externally fixed; downstream effects depend on these boundary conditions.

proposals.rationale: In the surviving state after EGFR/FGFR3 KO, TP53 and PTEN are active. TP53 drives p21CIP and MDM2; PTEN constrains AKT. Simultaneous knockout removes the survival signals (p21CIP, AKT activation) that keep the cell alive, and the model has a proven working set ['AKT', 'TP53'] suggesting this combination forces apoptosis.

The surviving state has RB1 and RBL2 active, which suppress E2F and block apoptosis. Knocking out TP53 (already known to cooperate with AKT) plus RBL2 removes the RB-mediated block on E2F, allowing the apoptotic pathway to proceed even with EGFR/FGFR3 present.

The surviving state after EGFR/FGFR3 KO keeps CHEK1_2 and ATM active, which maintain checkpoint survival signals. Combined with TP53 knockout, this removes the G2/M checkpoint and p53-mediated survival mechanisms, pushing the cell toward apoptosis.
